messages:
marco: quick sync — we keep hitting a weird failure mode where microbench spikes in intake cause admit to backpressure. thinking out loud about a lightweight compatibility gate we can run before full bench. any strong opinions?

ada: +1 we need a cheap pre-check. full bench is expensive and often unnecessary.

s.jensen: can you describe the failure mode? is it perf outlier or correctness?

marco: mostly perf: sudden 20x tail latency from certain model ops when sequence patterns include long recursions. bench catches it but by then we've created heavy load.

ivy: sounds like an opset/attention-kernel mismatch. suggest a two-stage flow: 1) lint/signature + opset check (cheap), 2) microbench smoke (short samples), 3) full bench if smoke passes.

ada: agree. stage 2 should be capped in tokens/time. i.e. sample N inputs, warmup M tokens, max 30s. enough to catch fat tails.

marco: draft rule: lint -> opset parity -> sample-microbench(100 samples, warmup=5) -> if p99/ms > threshold then fail fast. else schedule full bench offline. ok?

s.jensen: thresholds are tricky. propose dynamic threshold: percentile multiplier relative to golden-model baseline rather than absolute ms. less brittle across HW.

ivy: good call. store golden baselines per class (decoder-only, encoder-decoder) + seq len buckets. compare ratio > 3x triggers fail.

ada: need to decide where to run sample microbench: intake runner (fast but shared infra) vs dedicated canary pods. intake runner is cheaper but can interfere with live traffic.

marco: tradeoff: intake runner reduces latency to acceptance but risks load. canary pods cost more but isolate. maybe run sample microbench in intake but with strict cgroup/cpu limit and network QoS. if sample close to threshold, escalate to canary run.

s.jensen: implement as: intake-runner with RLIMITS + token cap; if ratio in [1.5,3) then route to canary for confirm. if >3 fail immediate.

ada: what about cache/KV parity checks? some regressions only show when kv cache grows. microbench samples should include prefix concat tests to exercise cache.

ivy: add 20% of samples synthetic long-prefix cases. mark them as KV-heavy.

marco: good. also need to track determinism: some ops change FLOPs after quantization; add a quick checksum-of-output for a small golden input to assert no catastrophic correctness drift.

s.jensen: checksum should be configurable per model family; fuzzy-match for float noise. use normalized-l2 < epsilon or token-level match for discrete tasks.

ada: rollout policy: if sample passes intake but full bench later fails, we should auto-create a rollback flag and prevent model from going GA. how do we surface this?

marco: console alert + tag model as "admit-blocked: postbench-regression" and open ticket auto with bench artifacts and heatmap.

ivy: infra-bot can create job with label bench-auto-debug and attach CPU/GPU profiles.

infra-bot: scheduled bench-auto-debug job for model=mdlr-2026-03 at 1712110500, assigned to bench-node-pool-canary. :robot_face:

marco: nice. one more: telemetry. we need per-check metrics + provenance: which runner, config, golden-bucket, HW. this helps tune thresholds.

ada: agreed. add trace id to every admission event. link to console bench heatmap.

s.jensen: finalizing action items: 1) ada - implement intake microbench wrapper with RLIMITS and synthetic KV samples (ETA 3d). 2) ivy - define golden baselines + bucket taxonomy (ETA 2d). 3) marco - console tag + rollback wiring + artifacts linking (ETA 4d). 4) infra - canary pool scheduling and bench-auto-debug job template (ETA 5d).

ivy: leaving small note: keep the microbench sample deterministic seed for reproducibility.

ada: cool. will also add CI gate tests so PRs modifying runner don't regress sample harness.

marco: thanks all. i'll open a follow-up RFC with config schemas and example YAMLs. for now i'll sketch the intake microbench config: 

```yaml
prebench:
  lint: true
  opset_check: true
  sample_microbench:
    samples: 100
    warmup: 5
    kv_heavy_pct: 20
    token_cap: 1000
    cpu_limit: 0.5
    threshold_ratio: 3.0
    escalate_ratio: 1.5
```

marco: putting this into the RFC draft. ping me if you want different knobs. :thumbsup:

ada: +1, thanks.

s.jensen: thanks — patch review incoming. :white_check_mark:
